data_sources.role: primary analysis file: one record per prisoner; outcome, rank, service, detaining power, camp, report date, unit
linked covariate file (enlisted Army personnel only): year of birth, education, dependency, height
camp geocoding for distance to detaining power's capital and for 'outside Germany/Japan proper' descriptive

unit_of_observation: Individual prisoner record (one row per record in nara_pow_rg389 after sample steps). Group-level regressors (hierarchy indices, group size) are computed over the prisoner's group and attached to each member.

sample_steps.description: Start from all records of the POW file.

locators.quote: The core data for our investigations come from the World War II Prisoners of War Data File

sample_steps.ambiguity: The article describes the file as containing records on American POWs; the registry file also contains some Allied civilians and internees (source description), which step 2 and 3 remove.

sample_steps.rule: Drop records with SERVICE_CODE in {'6' (CIVILIAN), '7' (WAR CORRESPONDENT)}. Keep '1' ARMY, '2' NAVY, '3' MARINE, '4' MERCHANT MARINE. Keep records whose SERVICE_CODE is blank or undefined (they are not identified as civilian).

locators.quote: we exclude from our analyses civilians
We also exclude civilians and those not held by either Germany or Japan
arm of service (Army, Navy, Marine, Merchant Marine, civilian, or war correspondent)

sample_steps.ambiguity: Whether Merchant Marine (code 4, civilian seamen) and war correspondents (code 7) count as 'civilians' is not stated; the article lists them as distinct categories. See specification axis A01. Treatment of blank/undefined SERVICE_CODE is not stated.

sample_steps.description: Exclude prisoners detained by neutral powers or by unidentified powers; keep only Germany and Japan.
sample_steps.rule: Keep records with DET_POWER in {'1' (GERMANY), '2' (JAPAN)}. Drop DET_POWER = '9' (others / neutral-country internment per NARA processing notes) and any blank or other value (unidentified power).

locators.quote: those detained by neutral powers (2,132) or by unidentified powers (3,204)

sample_steps.ambiguity: The code list defines only 1 and 2; the mapping neutral = '9', unidentified = blank/other follows NARA processing notes in the dictionary, not the article. Camp-code ranges (German 001-492, 801-951; Japanese 501-802) are not used to impute a missing detaining power.

sample_steps.description: Exclude prisoners whose survival status is unknown.
sample_steps.rule: Keep records with STA in {'4','5','7','8','9'}. Drop STA blank, '0' (meaning unknown per NARA) or any other value.

locators.quote: those for whom it is not known if they survived captivity
If it is unknown whether a POW survives captivity, he is excluded from our analyses.

sample_steps.ambiguity: None beyond the code list; hand-written card notes that contradict punched status are not usable.

sample_steps.description: Descriptive sample (Table 1 analogue) is the result of steps 1-4. Split by DET_POWER for the Germany and Japan columns.
sample_steps.rule: Sample after steps 1-4; Germany = DET_POWER '1'; Japan = DET_POWER '2'. Number of observations varies by item (covariates from the enlistment link are available only for matched records).

locators.quote: Number of observations varies with the data item.

sample_steps.description: Regression sample: require a usable camp code and a usable report month so that both camp cohort and captured cohort can be formed; use one common sample for all regression columns.
sample_steps.rule: From the step-4 sample keep records with CAMP not blank and CAMP != '000', and with DATE_REPORTED_MONTH in '01'..'12' and DATE_REPORTED_YEAR in {'1'..'6'}. Apply the same sample to every column of the main table and of the officer-interaction table.

locators.quote: The cohort regressions also include but do not report dummy variables for each POW camp.
Those POWs who enter the same camp in the same month.

sample_steps.ambiguity: The article never states this restriction; it is implied by the need to form cohorts and by the single observation count printed for all columns. The article's regression sample is smaller than its descriptive sample by an unexplained amount; this step is the reader's reconstruction. Whether the camp-cohort columns used a larger sample (not requiring the month) is unknown; see axis A02.

sample_steps.description: Link enlistment covariates by Army serial number (covariate construction only; no records are dropped for failing to match).
sample_steps.rule: Match SERIAL_NO (POW file, positions 1-8) to SER_NUM (enlistment file, positions 1-8) as exact 8-character strings after replacing '#' with blank in SER_NUM and trimming surrounding blanks in both. If several enlistment records share one serial number, treat the match as ambiguous and set all enlistment-derived covariates to missing. For enlistment records with CARD_NUM = '3' (E.R.C. statistical card) read YR_BIRTH/EDUCATION/MARITAL_STATUS/HEIGHT from the ERC_* slices; otherwise from the standard slices.

locators.quote: his serial number (which is how we merge it with the POW database)
yet we do not want to restrict our analyses to POWs who are in the enlistment database

sample_steps.ambiguity: Handling of duplicate serial numbers, of officer identity-code letters in SERIAL_NO (e.g. leading 'O'), and of the E.R.C. card layout is not described; see axis A10. Officers, Navy, Marine and pre-1938 enlistees cannot match by design.

sample_steps.description: Software-default sample loss in camp-fixed-effect probits.
sample_steps.rule: In captured-cohort regressions that include camp indicator variables, observations in camps where the outcome does not vary are dropped by the maximum-likelihood probit routine (perfect prediction). Record the number dropped; do not override unless the specification axis says so.

locators.quote: we use a dummy variable for each POW camp and then compare survival rates among cohorts within the same camp

sample_steps.ambiguity: Not discussed in the article; the single observation count reported for both fixed-effect and non-fixed-effect columns suggests either no camps were dropped or the count refers to the input sample. See axis A09.

variables.name: survival
variables.definition: 1 if the POW survives captivity, 0 if he dies in captivity.
variables.construction: survival = 1 if STA in {'7','8','9'}; survival = 0 if STA in {'4','5'}. Records with other STA values are excluded (sample step 4).

locators.quote: Takes a value of 1 if the POW survives captivity and 0 if he dies in captivity.

variables.ambiguity: STA '4' bundles executions, ship-sinking deaths and deaths while escaping; all are deaths in captivity.

variables.name: executed
variables.definition: 1 if the POW is reported as executed by the detaining power (descriptive only; also used for the 'exclude executions' robustness subset).
variables.construction: executed = 1 if STA = '4'; 0 otherwise.

locators.quote: Some executed by Japan died in 'hell ships.'

variables.ambiguity: Code 4 also covers 'shot while attempting escape' and ship-sinking deaths; the article's note about hell ships suggests it used this code as printed, but it is not stated.

variables.name: rank_value
variables.definition: Integer rank on a nine-level ladder: privates 1, corporals 2, sergeants 3, warrant officers 4, lieutenants 5, captains 6, majors 7, colonels 8, generals 9 (order of the rows of the article's illustrative table).
variables.construction: Primary source GRADE_ALPHA (pow_GRADE_ALPHA_cl1275.csv), with SERVICE_CODE used to resolve Navy/Marine abbreviations. Army/Marine mapping: Private, Private First Class, Aviation Cadet, Cadet -> 1; Corporal, Technician 5th Grade -> 2; all Sergeant grades (Sergeant, Staff, Technical, Master, First, Gunnery, Platoon, Sergeant Major, Technician 3d/4th Grade) -> 3; Warrant Officer, Warrant Officer Junior Grade, Chief Warrant Officer, Flight Officer -> 4; Second Lieutenant, First Lieutenant, Lieutenant -> 5; Captain -> 6; Major -> 7; Lieutenant Colonel, Colonel -> 8; Brigadier/Major/Lieutenant General, General -> 9. Navy (SERVICE_CODE '2') equivalents: Apprentice Seaman, Seaman 2nd/1st class, non-rated ratings (fireman etc.) -> 1; petty officer 3rd class ratings -> 2; petty officer 2nd/1st class and chief petty officer ratings -> 3; Warrant/Chief Warrant -> 4; Ensign, Lieutenant Junior Grade -> 5; Navy Lieutenant -> 6; Lieutenant Commander -> 7; Commander, Navy Captain -> 8; Rear/Vice Admiral, Admiral -> 9. Nurses, dietitians and contract surgeons: map by their relative-rank equivalents in the code list meaning (e.g. 'Second Lieutenant or Nurse' -> 5). Fallback when GRADE_ALPHA is blank or unmapped: use GRADE_CODE (pow_GRADE_CODE_cl1279.csv) together with the first character of SERIAL_NO ('O' or 'T' = officer identity code) to choose the officer or enlisted meaning of digit codes 1-9.
variables.missing_handling: Records with unmappable rank cannot contribute to hierarchy indices; treat rank as missing, exclude them from index computation but keep them in the regression sample with a missing indicator only if they would otherwise be in the sample (see missingness_rules). Flagged as ambiguity.

locators.quote: privates are assigned a value of 1, corporals a value of 2, and so on, up to generals who are assigned a value of 9

variables.ambiguity: The article does not say how the many grade abbreviations (including Navy/Marine grades and nurses) were collapsed into nine ranks; the mapping above is the reader's reconstruction consistent with the nine rows of the illustrative table. See axis A03.

variables.name: captured_cohort_id
variables.definition: Prisoners who enter the same camp in the same month.
variables.construction: captured_cohort_id = CAMP + '-' + DATE_REPORTED_YEAR + '-' + DATE_REPORTED_MONTH, formed on the regression sample.
variables.missing_handling: records with blank CAMP or invalid month/year excluded (sample step 6)

locators.quote: Those POWs who enter the same camp in the same month.
those prisoners who enter a given POW camp during the same month ('captured cohort')

variables.ambiguity: The POW file has no 'date entered camp' field; the 'date reported' (DDMMY) is the only capture-side date and is assumed to proxy the month of entry. The article elsewhere calls it 'date of capture'.

variables.name: camp_cohort_id
variables.definition: The camp where the POW is initially incarcerated.
variables.construction: camp_cohort_id = CAMP (three-character code), formed on the regression sample.

locators.quote: The camp where the POW is initially incarcerated.

variables.ambiguity: NARA notes the camp may be the first or last camp; codes 359 and 510 have two meanings (treated as single codes).

variables.name: steepness
variables.definition: Ordered Gini coefficient of rank values within the group (captured cohort or camp cohort depending on the model).
variables.construction: For each group g with n members sorted so that rank_value is nondescending and indexed indiv = 1..n: steepness_g = 1 + 1/n - (2 * sum_{indiv=1}^{n} (n + 1 - indiv) * rank_value_indiv) / (n * sum_{indiv=1}^{n} rank_value_indiv). Groups are formed over the records in the regression sample with non-missing rank_value (see axis A04).
variables.missing_handling: members with missing rank_value are excluded from the computation; if a group has no member with a rank, steepness is missing and handled by missingness_rules

locators.quote: Steepness of Hierarchy is measured with an ordered Gini coefficient following Damgaard and Weiner (2000).

variables.ambiguity: Whether the population over which groups are formed is the regression sample, the descriptive sample, or all records in the file is not stated (axis A04).

variables.name: sameness
variables.definition: One minus the scaled sum over the nine ranks of squared deviations between the group's rank fractions and the population rank fractions.
variables.construction: population_fraction_r = share of members with rank_value = r among all records in the descriptive sample (steps 1-4) with non-missing rank_value, for r = 1..9. For each group g: sameness_g = 1 - (1/1.319) * sum_{r=1}^{9} (group_fraction_{g,r} - population_fraction_r)^2, where group_fraction_{g,r} is the share of group members with rank_value = r.

locators.quote: We use 1.319 to scale the sum of the squared deviations because that number ensures that the hierarchy measure will equal 0 for the least hierarchical group.
we use the percentage of soldiers in each rank from the population of American POWs during World War II.

variables.ambiguity: The population used for the fractions (descriptive sample vs regression sample vs whole file) is not stated; the constant 1.319 is printed, while its stated rationale implies it equals (1 - p_9)^2 + sum_{r<9} p_r^2 for the population fractions used (axis A05).

variables.name: men_in_hierarchy
variables.definition: Natural log of the number of POWs in the captured cohort or the camp cohort, depending on the specification; rescaled.
variables.construction: men_in_hierarchy = ln(n_g) / 10 where n_g is the number of records in group g (same group population as the hierarchy indices).
variables.missing_handling: never missing within the regression sample

locators.row: Men in captured or camp cohort
locators.quote: The natural log of the number of POWs in either the captured cohort (defined below) or the camp cohort depending on the regression specification. Rescaled in both cases (divided by 10).

variables.ambiguity: Whether n_g counts all file records in the group or only sample records (axis A04).

variables.name: men_in_hierarchy_sq
variables.definition: Square of men_in_hierarchy.
variables.construction: men_in_hierarchy_sq = (men_in_hierarchy)^2 = (ln(n_g)/10)^2.

locators.quote: We include a squared term to capture possible nonlinearities in the relation between hierarchy size and survival.

variables.ambiguity: Whether the square is taken after or before rescaling is not stated; after rescaling assumed.

variables.name: distance_to_capital
variables.definition: Natural log of kilometers from the camp to the national capital of the relevant detaining power (Berlin for DET_POWER '1', Tokyo for DET_POWER '2'); camps in Berlin or Tokyo get ln(1) = 0; rescaled.
variables.construction: Join CAMP to camp_location_crosswalk.camp_code; take latitude, longitude (decimal degrees). Capital coordinates: Berlin 52.5200 N, 13.4050 E; Tokyo 35.6762 N, 139.6503 E. Distance km = great-circle (haversine) distance with Earth radius 6371 km. If identified_place_name is Berlin (DET_POWER '1') or Tokyo (DET_POWER '2'), set distance = 1 km. distance_to_capital = ln(distance km) / 10. If confidence = 'unknown' or coordinates are empty, the variable is missing.

locators.row: Distance from camp to Berlin or Tokyo
locators.quote: If the camp is in either Berlin or Tokyo, we use the natural log of one kilometer. Rescaled (divided by 10).

variables.ambiguity: Distance formula, camp coordinates source and capital coordinates are not stated by the article; the crosswalk schema requires the manifest to state them (axis A07). Only used in camp-cohort specifications.

variables.name: length_of_captivity
variables.definition: Number of months before the end of the war that the POW was captured; war ends May 1945 in Europe and September 1945 in the Pacific; rescaled.
variables.construction: year = 1940 + integer(DATE_REPORTED_YEAR) (code 1 = 1941 ... 6 = 1946); month = integer(DATE_REPORTED_MONTH). end_month = 5 and end_year = 1945 if DET_POWER = '1'; end_month = 9 and end_year = 1945 if DET_POWER = '2'. months = (end_year - year) * 12 + (end_month - month). length_of_captivity = months / 10.
variables.missing_handling: invalid month/year -> excluded by sample step 6; negative months (report date after war end) set to missing -> 0 plus missing indicator

locators.quote: The number of months before the end of the war the POW was captured. We classify the war as ending in Europe in May 1945; we classify the war as ending in the Pacific in September 1945.

variables.ambiguity: The article uses 'date of capture'; the file's 'date reported' is the proxy. Treatment of report dates after the war-end month (e.g. reports in 1946) is not described; set to missing here.

variables.name: height
variables.definition: Height in inches when entering the armed services; rescaled.
variables.construction: From the linked enlistment record: HEIGHT (positions 74-75) for standard cards, ERC_HEIGHT (75-76) for E.R.C. cards (CARD_NUM = '3'). Parse as integer inches; values that are non-numeric, '##', 0, or outside 48-84 are set to missing. height = inches / 10.

locators.quote: Height of POW in inches when entering the Armed Services. Rescaled (divided by 10).

variables.ambiguity: NARA could not date when columns 74-78 carried height/weight versus other content; the plausibility window 48-84 inches is the reader's choice. Unmatched POWs (officers, Navy, Marines, pre-1938 enlistees) are missing by construction.

variables.name: age
variables.definition: Age in years as of 1945; rescaled.
variables.construction: birth_year = 1900 + integer(YR_BIRTH) (or ERC_YR_BIRTH for E.R.C. cards); age_years = 1945 - birth_year; set to missing if YR_BIRTH is non-numeric or age_years is outside 15-70. age = age_years / 100.

locators.quote: Age of POW in number of years as of 1945. Rescaled (divided by 100).

variables.ambiguity: Century assumption (19YY) and plausibility window are the reader's.

variables.name: education
variables.definition: Years of education beyond eighth grade completed upon entering the armed services; rescaled.
variables.construction: From EDUCATION (or ERC_EDUCATION) code (asnf_EDUCATION_cl2058.csv): '0' Grammar school -> 0; '1'..'4' = that many years of high school -> 1..4; '5'..'8' = 1..4 years of college -> 5..8; '9' Post-graduate -> 9. Other characters -> missing. education = years / 10.

locators.quote: Number of years of education beyond eighth grade completed by POW upon entering the armed services. Rescaled (divided by 10).

variables.ambiguity: The number of years assigned to 'Post-graduate' is not stated (axis A06). Grammar school (possibly fewer than 8 years) is coded 0.

variables.name: has_dependents
variables.definition: 1 if the POW has dependents, 0 otherwise.
variables.construction: From MARITAL_STATUS (or ERC_MARITAL_STATUS) code (asnf_MARITAL_STATUS_cl2081.csv): '1' single with dependents, '3' separated with dependents, '4' divorced with dependents, '5' widowed with dependents, and '2' married -> 1; '6','7','8','9' (without dependents) -> 0; other -> missing.

locators.quote: Takes a value of 1 if POW has dependents and 0 otherwise.

variables.ambiguity: The code 'Married' carries no dependency qualifier; treating married men as having dependents is the reader's assumption (axis A08).

variables.name: is_officer
variables.definition: 1 if the POW is ranked lieutenant or higher at the time of capture.
variables.construction: is_officer = 1 if rank_value >= 5; 0 if rank_value in 1..4; missing if rank_value missing.

locators.quote: Takes a value of 1 if the POW is ranked lieutenant or higher at the time of capture.

variables.ambiguity: Warrant and flight officers (rank 4) are not officers under this definition.

formulas.name: Steepness of Hierarchy (ordered Gini)
formulas.latex_or_text: S_g = 1 + \frac{1}{n} - \frac{2\sum_{indiv=1}^{n}(n+1-indiv)\,Rank_{indiv}}{n\sum_{indiv=1}^{n}Rank_{indiv}}, members indexed in nondescending order of rank
formulas.inputs: rank_value of each member of group g; n = group size

formulas.name: Sameness of Hierarchy
formulas.inputs: group rank shares; population rank shares (from the POW population); constant 1.319

formulas.name: Great-circle distance (reader-specified)
formulas.inputs: camp latitude/longitude from crosswalk; capital coordinates Berlin (52.5200, 13.4050), Tokyo (35.6762, 139.6503)

locators.row: Distance from camp to Berlin or Tokyo

formulas.name: Probit marginal effect at means
formulas.latex_or_text: Continuous x_k: \partial P/\partial x_k = \phi(\bar{x}'\beta)\beta_k. Dummy x_k: \Phi(\bar{x}_{-k}'\beta_{-k} + \beta_k) - \Phi(\bar{x}_{-k}'\beta_{-k}), other regressors at their sample means
formulas.inputs: probit coefficients; sample means of all regressors including unreported dummies

locators.quote: The coefficients report the change in the probability for an infinitesimal change in the continuous variables and the discrete change in the probability for the dummy variables.
Table 4 reports the marginal effects of a probit regression at the means of the independent variables.

missingness_rules: Outcome, detaining power, camp and report month must be non-missing (sample steps). For every independent variable that can be missing (height, age, education, has_dependents, is_officer, distance_to_capital, length_of_captivity, friends and, if applicable, a hierarchy index), replace the missing value by 0 and add an unreported indicator equal to 1 when missing. Unmatched POWs (no enlistment record) therefore remain in the sample with all enlistment-derived covariates set to 0 and their indicators set to 1. Robustness subset (a) of M31 instead drops any observation with a missing covariate.

inference_rules.test: z-test of each probit coefficient (equivalently of its marginal effect) using heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors clustered by captured cohort (captured-cohort models) or by camp cohort (camp-cohort models); p-values reported to two decimals. ROC incremental tests per Hanley and McNeil (1983).
inference_rules.tail: two (assumed; the article does not state the tail)
inference_rules.notes: The article treats p <= 0.10 as 'marginally significant'.
